refnamediv.refpurpose: Creates or open a shared memory segment

refentry.refsect1:
&reftitle.description;
SysvSharedMemoryfalseshm_attach intkey intnullsize&null; intpermissions0666
shm_attach returns an id that can be used to access the System V shared memory with the given key, the first call creates the shared memory segment with size and the optional perm-bits permissions.
A second call to shm_attach for the same key will return a different SysvSharedMemory instance, but both instances access the same underlying shared memory. size and permissions will be ignored.
The segment survives the end of the script and of the SysvSharedMemory instance; it is only removed by shm_remove. If an existing segment was not created by shm_attach, its first bytes are overwritten with the header of the extension.

&reftitle.parameters;
key
A numeric System V IPC key, for example the result of ftok. It is not the identifier of the segment.
size
The memory size, in bytes, of the whole segment: the data area is 40 bytes smaller on 64-bit builds, and a segment that does not exist yet cannot be created with a smaller size. If not provided, default to the sysvshm.init_mem in the &php.ini;, otherwise 10000 bytes.
permissions
The optional permission bits, used only when the segment is created. Default to 0666, which makes the segment readable and writable by every local user.

&reftitle.returnvalues;
Returns a SysvSharedMemory instance on success, or &false; on failure. An E_WARNING is emitted when the segment cannot be created or attached, for example when size is too small for a new segment or the system call fails. When several processes create the same segment at the same time, the one that loses the race fails with a File exists warning.
